title: Use skills rather than the prime hook
description:
_Promoted from Fleece branch-local working memory._

- [ ] **pt4hHj** Use skills rather than the prime hook _(task)_

  Split, don't swap: move the static reference content of `fleece prime` into an installable skill, but keep a slim, state-aware SessionStart hook.

  Background: the `fleece install` hook currently runs `fleece prime` on every SessionStart, which bundles two different things: (1) static reference (the 9 topics + workflow overview) and (2) a dynamic proactive signal — CountActiveIssuesAsync() emitting 'N active issue(s) on this branch; branch must be clean before merge', which arms awareness of the CI gate.

  Skills are pull-based (loaded only when the agent already senses relevance), so they fit (1) but fundamentally cannot deliver (2): an agent that doesn't know active issues exist has no trigger to invoke the skill. A pure skill swap silently drops the CI-gate tripwire.

  Plan:
  - Move the static topics (hierarchy, commands, statuses, sync, json, next, tree, github, v4-migration) + workflow detail into a skill installed by `fleece install`. Removes duplication with the CLAUDE.md memory block.
  - Shrink the SessionStart hook to ONLY the dynamic state, and emit nothing when activeCount == 0 (clean branch -> ~0 tokens/session vs ~2k today). Dirty branch -> 2-line warning + pointer to the skill.

  Net: fewer tokens on clean sessions, same CI-gate safety signal on dirty ones, reference content where it belongs.
